title: One entitlement decision can serve reports and chat
assumptions: This diagram presents the intended congruent future design: existing application login and current entitlements inform both report and conversational access to shared business measures and RLS intent.

Zones describe logical responsibilities, not subnets, deployments or strict tenancy boundaries. The topology represents two converging lanes with large labels, not a detailed runtime protocol sequence.

The conversational path is a custom broker design, not native Fabric IQ app-only support. No new end-user Entra accounts are introduced; the separate delegated IQ schema caller is outside this diagram.
evidence_gaps: Actual Embedded-versus-chat parity has not been run; Embedded/report parity is not yet observed.
Roles and identity-field/RLS expressions must be aligned before claiming one unchanged role works in both paths: current Embedded may use USERNAME(), while the proof uses a CUSTOMDATA()-based role.

Documented EffectiveIdentity customData support for cloud models and executeDaxQueries customData support do not establish compatibility with this particular customer model. The required workspace-admin status for a service principal selecting roles is a prerequisite, not a verified customer permission.

zones.label: Application
zones.description: Logical responsibility for existing application authorization and the custom conversational query broker. External denotes application responsibility relative to the shared model, not a deployment or network boundary.

zones.label: Report experience
zones.description: Logical responsibility for the app-owns-data Embedded report experience, abstracting backend token generation and browser report consumption.

zones.label: Shared semantic model
zones.description: Logical responsibility for shared business measures and intended RLS enforcement across both query paths; no strict tenancy claim is implied.

nodes.label: Application authorization
nodes.notes: Existing login and current entitlements supply the application authorization decision. The diagram distinguishes the Embedded effective-identity path from the trusted role and app-user key passed to the broker; it does not prescribe a new identity provider.

nodes.label: Power BI
nodes.notes: Embedded report path using app-owns-data. This node abstracts both the normal backend GenerateToken operation, performed using an Entra access token, and browser consumption of the embedded report using the resulting embed token. The incoming identity edge summarizes that handoff rather than depicting a separate token-generation service. An embed token is for report consumption, not a generic REST API credential.

nodes.label: Custom query broker
nodes.notes: Proposed conversational path. The broker authenticates with a service principal and calls executeDaxQueries with roles and customData, not an embed token. The proof binds the trusted app-user key outside LLM arguments and uses a CUSTOMDATA()-based model role. A service principal selecting roles must be a workspace admin; that permission is not asserted as already granted. No embed-token authentication for executeDaxQueries or Fabric IQ is implied.

nodes.label: Semantic Model
nodes.notes: Shared business measures and RLS intent for report and conversational queries. Equivalent enforcement is an intended outcome, not observed parity. Align the identity-field and role-expression contract, including potential Embedded USERNAME() versus proof CUSTOMDATA() differences, before claiming one unchanged role serves both paths.
